verdicts.trueWording: Martin's evocative storytelling style and gift for gripping narrative are mostly absent from this dry history
verdicts.note: Opening sentence of the PW review, fetched raw from publishersweekly.com (HTTP 200). Quote appears word for word; every limb ('evocative storytelling style', 'gift for gripping narrative', 'mostly absent', 'dry history') is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: mostly gives rise to images of unhappy Westerosi schoolchildren being forced to study this weighty textbook
verdicts.note: Raw PW review. Page: 'The conceit of the history being written by one Archmaester Gyldayn ... mostly gives rise to images of unhappy Westerosi schoolchildren being forced to study this weighty textbook.' Gyldayn attribution, schoolchildren and weighty textbook all present.

verdicts.trueWording: Brief sections are dramatic ('the golden dragon devoured the queen in six bites')
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim on the raw PW page, but the review assigns that image to the BRIEF DRAMATIC sections and explicitly contrasts them with summary: 'they only last a few pages before a return to brisk summary.' The page does not say the summary voice lands such images; it says the opposite relation.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the SUMMARY voice lands these concrete images - the review credits them to brief dramatic sections set against 'brisk summary'

verdicts.trueWording: he has prejudices and gripes and his own cavils, and you have to realize that you're reading the voice of a character
verdicts.note: Raw PW interview (gzip-decoded, HTTP 200). Page: Gyldayn 'is an opinionated guy and has his views of these people, that definitely leak into it. Every limb supported; page says 'guy' where the claim says 'man'.

verdicts.trueWording: some of my readers actually took umbrage ... they felt that it was demeaning
verdicts.note: Raw PW interview. Page: 'I was using the term "fake history" for a number of years, and some of my readers actually took umbrage at that. They didn't like the term-they felt that it was demeaning ... So I thought imaginary history was a good way to describe it.' Drop of the term, the umbrage and the demeaning label are all on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: an entirely different literary form than what's essentially a popular history
